Hi Sergio,

Thank you for the demo last week. We’re excited about Redwood’s private deployment option — it ticks the boxes for our compliance needs. We have two asks from procurement before we move forward: a) a commercial structure that reduces our unit cost during ramp (we expect usage to be lumpy for the first 9 months) and b) an onboarding credit to offset migration costs.

Our finance team has a constrained budget this quarter and has signaled they need a 40–50% reduction off list for the first 12 months to make the numbers work. That’s probably wider than you normally do, but I wanted to surface it early and see what flexibility exists.

Can you share what concessions Redwood can offer for a 2-year commitment (private VPC + dedicated capacity) if we sign by end of Q1? Also attach any term sheet drafts you can.

Best,
Elaine

Lumina Therapeutics

High-level offer we can carry to procurement (subject to internal approval):

Subject: Lumina Therapeutics — request for exception: onboarding credit + floor waiver (CFO signoff requested)

Team,

I’m escalating a request from Lumina (prospect moving to pilot → production). Key points:
- Opportunity: 2-year private deployment (VPC + dedicated GPUs) — estimated ARR if converted ~ $1.8M over 24 months; first-year ARR run-rate ~ $820k.
- Ask from Lumina: 40–50% reduction off list for first 12 months. My initial counter (attached) is 25% per-token reduction + 20% onboarding credit; Lumina has asked we consider more since they have budget pressure.
- Special requirement: Regulated biotech; private deployment + SOC2/controls are must-haves — high strategic value and reference potential in life sciences vertical.

Why to approve:
- Net present value still positive vs. building private infra themselves; retention probability high once integrated (sticky integration + compliance).
- Competitive pressure: a competitor has offered steep initial credits. If we don’t move, risk losing to that vendor.

Proposed exception (what I’m asking you to approve):
1) One-time onboarding credit = 30% of month-1 expected bill (capped at $150k).
2) Per-token rate discount = 18% for months 1–12, revert to standard list thereafter.
3) Waive the 6-month commitment floor for year 1 and replace with a soft-usage guardrail: if monthly usage falls below 40% of forecast for >2 consecutive months, we’ll re-evaluate pricing (not immediate financial penalty).

Financial impact / guardrails:
- Expected concession cap (worst case) ~ $200k total over first 12 months (we cap onboarding credit and have discount end at month 12).
- Require mandatory billing checkpoints at M3 and M6 with finance to reconcile realized usage vs. forecast and apply clawback if usage materially deviates after month 12.

Requested approvals:
- Marissa: commercial approval and signoff on rates
- Markus: executive approval for floor waiver + final threshold caps
- Vanessa: finance/CFO review for concession cap and accounting treatment (need DocuSign flow to reflect cap)

I’ve attached the term sheet and usage forecast. If approved, I’ll send a revised term sheet and route to DocuSign. Lumina is expecting an answer by EOD Monday (2027-02-15).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the unit economics.

Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
